newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila tuna exporter First Dominion plans IPO.
newsitem.headline: Manila tuna exporter First Dominion plans IPO.

text.p: Canned tuna exporter First Dominion Prime Holdings Inc said on Wednesday it is planning an initial public offering (IPO) of shares.

First Dominion president Jonathan Dee told reporters the company is preparing registration papers for a medium-sized IPO within the year or by middle 1998 to finance in part the construction of additional tuna canning facilities.
Dee said the facilities may be set up in the southern Philippines where 45 percent of the world's tuna stocks can be found.
First Dominion has four tuna canning facilities and by the end of the year a one billion peso facility in the southern city of General Santos will be ready for commercial operation.
Dee said he expects the company to post a net income of 125 million pesos in 1996 from 110 million pesos in 1995.
Revenues for 1997 are expected to double from 1.8 billion pesos in 1996.
The United States accounts for 80 percent of the company's total sales.
First Dominion is 75 percent owned by the Dee family which has substantial stake in China Banking Corp.
